title: Stop paying for CCA runs that cannot decide anything
outcome: A pull request stops spawning duplicate and structurally-doomed Completion Check Agent runs. Measured 2026-08-17: shiki ran 200 CCA runs over 154 distinct head SHAs (1.30x, 27 pairs starting within 3 minutes of each other on the same SHA); CubeShare ran 200 over 135 (1.48x, 46 near-simultaneous pairs, worst SHAs at 4 runs each). On 2026-08-10 alone CubeShare's Shiki CCA Completion workflow consumed 523 wall-clock minutes across 74 runs. Three causes are removed here, and the one coupling that would make the fix actively harmful is removed with them, in the same commit.

The operator instructed 'CCA の再実行問題を先に潰し' and then approved this contract as enumerated (scope, non-goals, locks, acceptance checks, risk medium) before any plan file existed. grill_with_docs.source: Measured 2026-08-17 against shiki origin/main (1dd1be7) and mizutani-140/CubeShare (72c96e59) via the GitHub Actions API and the workflow sources at origin/main.
decisions: CAUSE 1, MEASURED — no concurrency control exists anywhere. `grep -c '^concurrency:'` returns 0 for all five of shiki-cca-completion.yml, shiki-mergegate.yml, shiki-validate.yml, shiki-claude-review.yml and shiki-orchestrator.yml. Consequence measured over the last 200 CCA runs in each repository: shiki 200 runs / 154 distinct head SHAs = 1.30x with 27 pairs starting within 180 seconds of each other on the SAME SHA; CubeShare 200 / 135 = 1.48x with 46 such pairs and five SHAs carrying 4 runs each. A superseded run is never cancelled, so every duplicate is a full Claude judgement paid for in runner minutes.

CAUSE 2, MEASURED — every label application spawns a full CCA run. Both shiki-cca-completion.yml and shiki-mergegate.yml declare `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, edited, labeled, unlabeled]`. Measured on shiki PR #323, head b635454c: the issue timeline records `07:35:29 labeled mergegate:contract` and `07:37:25 labeled guardian:approved`, and the CCA run list shows runs on that same SHA at 07:35, 07:35 and 07:37. The sanctioned Contract Approval procedure applies two labels, so it costs two extra CCA runs (~14 minutes) per contract PR by construction.

CAUSE 3, MEASURED — CCA-06 cannot pass on a PR's first run. `docs/agents/checklists.md:183` defines CCA-06 as 'Required checks pass on current head SHA.' with severity `blocking`. The CCA job reads check state exactly once, at the top of its own run: the `Prepare CCA context` step runs `gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --json number,title,body,author,headRefName,baseRefName,headRefOid,labels,files,reviews,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup > .shiki/gha/pr.json`. Because the CCA workflow triggers on the same `pull_request` event as CI, Validate and MergeGate, those checks are still pending in that rollup. The first run therefore cannot return `complete`, and a human re-run is required. This is the ordering defect, not a checklist defect — CCA-06 must stay blocking.

THE COUPLING THAT MAKES A NAIVE FIX HARMFUL. `scripts/shiki_loop.py:580` classifies check conclusions: `if value in {"pass","success"}: return "pass"` / `if value in {"pending","queued","in_progress"}: return "pending"` / `return "fail"`. A `cancelled` conclusion therefore falls through to `fail`. Adding `cancel-in-progress` WITHOUT widening this bucket makes the loop read every superseded CCA run as a failed required check and dispatch a repair against it — the exact 'repair attempts burned on a failure no implementer touched' class already recorded in this repository. The concurrency block and the `_check_bucket` widening MUST land in one commit. Splitting them makes the loop strictly worse than today.

LABEL FILTERING MUST NOT DROP THE APPROVAL LABELS. CCA-08 is 'Risk and policy-backed Guardian requirements from .shiki/guardian-policy.json are satisfied' (checklists.md:185), and `guardian:approved` is a Guardian approval source. Removing `labeled` outright, or filtering it in a way that excludes `guardian:approved`, would leave CCA permanently unable to observe an approval and would pin the verdict at needs_guardian. GitHub cannot filter by label name in `on:`, so the filter belongs in a job-level `if:` — a skipped job costs no runner minutes.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE — moving CCA to a `workflow_run` trigger. It removes the wait entirely, but `workflow_run` executes in the default-branch context with a write-capable token, which is the same class of exposure AGENTS.md warns about for `pull_request_target` ('Avoid pull_request_target unless the repository has explicitly accepted the security tradeoff'). Waiting inside the existing `pull_request` job keeps the current trust boundary. Recorded as rejected, not deferred.

SAFETY INVARIANT THAT MUST SURVIVE. The `CCA Review Bridge` step submits `--arg event "APPROVE"`. No step that posts a review, a comment or a label may gain `if: always()` in this task. The existing `if: always()` on `Upload CCA evidence` (a pure artifact upload) is unaffected and stays.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-17). MUST-CHANGE: the five workflow files; `scripts/shiki_loop.py` (the `_check_bucket` widening); `tests/test_loop_engine.py` (drives `decide_task_action` over check buckets); `tests/test_workflow_invocation.py` — this file reconstructs `mergegate_check.py`'s argv from the workflow `run:` steps and raises KeyError without a matching `_FLAG_VALUES` entry, so a new `run:` step in a locked workflow can break it and it must be inside the locks, not merely in the test command; and `tests/test_cca_rerun_economy.py` (new).

MUST-NOT-BREAK (verification command, not locks): `scripts/test_shiki_workflow_lint.sh`, which lints workflow structure and is the surface a new `concurrency:` block would trip; `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh`, which drives the loop end to end; `scripts/validate_shiki.py`, which enforces required workflow flags and pinned action versions; and `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, which must not be touched.

Risk is medium: this changes workflow triggering mechanics and one classification helper. No gate rule, schema, approval source, checklist severity or verdict semantic moves. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) this PR does not trigger the Guardian gate.

ORDERING. This task locks `.github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml` and `.github/workflows/shiki-mergegate.yml`, which the approved reflux task P1 also locks. The two cannot run in parallel and this one runs first, by operator instruction ('CCA の再実行問題を先に潰し').

non_goals: Moving CCA to a workflow_run trigger — rejected on the trust-boundary grounds recorded above.
Removing `labeled` from the CCA trigger, or filtering it in any way that excludes guardian:approved or the mergegate:* mode labels.
Changing CCA-06's severity, wording, or any checklist item in docs/agents/checklists.md.
Changing what the CCA judge evaluates, the verdict schema, or any verdict value.
Adding if: always() to any step that posts a review, a comment or a label — the CCA Review Bridge submits APPROVE.
Changing the repair attempt limit, or any MergeGate rule.
Deleting or disabling the Shiki Claude Review workflow — a separate decision, recorded but not taken here.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
completion_conditions: A superseded run on the same pull request is cancelled rather than run to completion.
A cancelled required check never causes the loop to dispatch a repair.
A label that is not an approval or mode label does not start a CCA job.
The CCA judge does not start while the required checks it must read are still pending.
No step that posts a review, comment or label gained if: always().
The full suite, the workflow lint, the goal-loop suite and validate_shiki stay green.

tasks.title: Cancel superseded runs, gate CCA on settled checks, and stop reading a cancelled check as a failure
tasks.scope:
Remove three measured causes of redundant Completion Check Agent runs, and the one coupling that would make the first of them harmful.

(a) CONCURRENCY. Add a `concurrency:` block with `cancel-in-progress: true` to all five workflows: shiki-cca-completion.yml, shiki-mergegate.yml, shiki-validate.yml, shiki-claude-review.yml, shiki-orchestrator.yml. Key the group per workflow and per pull request so that a newer event supersedes an older run on the SAME pull request and never touches a different one — `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}` is the intended shape. Measured today: `grep -c '^concurrency:'` is 0 in all five; shiki runs 200 CCA runs over 154 distinct head SHAs (27 pairs within 180s on the same SHA) and CubeShare 200 over 135 (46 such pairs, five SHAs at 4 runs).

(b) THE COUPLING — SAME COMMIT AS (a), NOT A SEPARATE ONE. `scripts/shiki_loop.py:580` `_check_bucket` returns "fail" for anything outside {pass, success} and {pending, queued, in_progress}. A `cancelled` conclusion therefore reads as a FAILED required check, and the loop dispatches a repair against a run that was merely superseded. Widen the non-terminal bucket to also cover `cancelled`, `skipped` and `stale`. Landing (a) without (b) makes the loop strictly worse than it is today: it converts every cancellation into a wasted repair attempt.

(c) LABEL FILTERING. Both shiki-cca-completion.yml and shiki-mergegate.yml trigger on `labeled` and `unlabeled`, so every label costs a full run. Measured on shiki PR #323 head b635454c: the timeline shows `07:35:29 labeled mergegate:contract` and `07:37:25 labeled guardian:approved`, and CCA ran at 07:35, 07:35 and 07:37. GitHub cannot filter by label name in `on:`, so add a JOB-LEVEL `if:` that proceeds only when the event is not a label event, or when the label is one that can change the verdict. `guardian:approved` and every `mergegate:*` mode label MUST remain in that set — CCA-08 reads the Guardian approval source, and removing it would pin the verdict at needs_guardian forever. A skipped job costs no runner minutes.

(d) SETTLED-CHECK GATE. The `Prepare CCA context` step reads check state once, at the top of its own run: `gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --json ...,statusCheckRollup > .shiki/gha/pr.json`. Because CCA triggers on the same `pull_request` event as CI, Validate and MergeGate, those checks are still pending, and CCA-06 ('Required checks pass on current head SHA.', blocking, checklists.md:183) cannot pass. Before the judge is invoked, wait until the required checks other than CCA's own have reached a terminal conclusion on the current head, with a bounded timeout and a clear message when the timeout is hit. Do NOT relax CCA-06 — this is an ordering fix, not a judgement fix. Do NOT move the workflow to a `workflow_run` trigger; that was considered and rejected on trust-boundary grounds.

MUST NOT: add `if: always()` to any step that posts a review, comment or label — the `CCA Review Bridge` step submits `--arg event "APPROVE"` and an always-run bridge would mint an approval on a refused verdict. Do not change docs/agents/checklists.md, the verdict schema, any verdict value, the repair attempt limit, any MergeGate rule, or scripts/mergegate_check.py. Do not delete or disable the Shiki Claude Review workflow.

TESTS. `tests/test_cca_rerun_economy.py` (new): all five workflows parse and each declares `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` and a group expression that includes the pull request number; the CCA and MergeGate jobs' `if:` admits `guardian:approved` and each `mergegate:*` mode label and rejects an unrelated label such as `documentation`; no step whose `run:` or `uses:` posts a review, comment or label carries `if: always()`. `tests/test_loop_engine.py`: `_check_bucket` maps `cancelled`, `skipped` and `stale` to the non-terminal bucket while `failure` and an unknown value still map to fail, and `decide_task_action` does not dispatch a repair for a PR whose only non-green required check is cancelled. `tests/test_workflow_invocation.py` reconstructs mergegate_check.py's argv from the workflow `run:` steps and raises KeyError without a matching `_FLAG_VALUES` entry — keep it green; if a new `run:` step changes what it parses, update it without weakening any existing assertion.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a single head SHA accumulates two to four full Claude CCA runs, each several minutes, and the first run on any new head cannot return `complete` no matter what the implementation does, so a human re-runs it by hand.
  Measured 2026-08-17: shiki 200 runs / 154 SHAs = 1.30x (27 near-simultaneous same-SHA pairs); CubeShare 200 / 135 = 1.48x (46 pairs, worst SHA 4 runs); CubeShare's CCA workflow consumed 523 minutes over 74 runs on 2026-08-10 alone.
  Root causes: no `concurrency:` in any of the five workflows; `labeled`/`unlabeled` in the CCA and MergeGate trigger types with no label filter; and a CCA job that reads `statusCheckRollup` at the top of a run that starts concurrently with the very checks CCA-06 requires to be green.
  Trap that makes a partial fix harmful: `shiki_loop.py:580` buckets `cancelled` as `fail`, so cancellation without the bucket widening converts each superseded run into a dispatched repair.
  Reproducible when: a second push or label on a pull request cancels the in-flight run instead of adding one; a cancelled check leaves the loop's decision unchanged; an unrelated label starts nothing; and the judge does not start while the checks it reads are pending.
non_goals: Moving CCA to a workflow_run trigger
Removing labeled from the CCA trigger, or excluding guardian:approved or any mergegate:* label from the filter
Changing CCA-06's severity or any entry in docs/agents/checklists.md
Changing the verdict schema, any verdict value, or what the judge evaluates
Adding if: always() to any step that posts a review, comment or label
Changing the repair attempt limit or any MergeGate rule
Deleting or disabling the Shiki Claude Review workflow
Touching any file outside the declared locks
acceptance_checks: All five workflows declare a concurrency block with cancel-in-progress: true and a group expression that distinguishes pull requests from one another.
_check_bucket maps cancelled, skipped and stale to the non-terminal bucket, and still maps failure and an unrecognised value to fail.
decide_task_action does not dispatch a repair for a PR whose only non-green required check is cancelled — asserted through the decision function, not by inspection.
A labeled event carrying guardian:approved starts the CCA job.
A labeled event carrying any mergegate:* mode label starts the CCA job.
A labeled event carrying an unrelated label does not start the CCA job.
The CCA judge step does not execute while a required check other than CCA's own is still pending on the current head, and the wait is bounded with a clear timeout message.
CCA-06 remains blocking and docs/agents/checklists.md is unchanged.
No step that posts a review, comment or label carries if: always(); the CCA Review Bridge in particular does not.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, scripts/test_shiki_workflow_lint.sh, scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh and validate_shiki all pass.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
tasks.test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target . && bash scripts/test_shiki_workflow_lint.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh
